figures.title: b3 audit robust
figures.caption: Corridors tested under four variants of the audit: the original Welch test with BH control against tests that respect dependence between legs of one recurring service; none of the 273 slower corridors clears the strictest. Source: b3_audit_robust.json

figures.title: b4 eb shrinkage
figures.caption: Empirical-Bayes posterior means against raw corridor means: shrinkage moves a corridor by only about 1% because corridor sampling variance is small against between-corridor variance. Source: b4_eb_ranking.json

figures.title: b4 eb stability heatmap
figures.caption: Top-20 overlap between support floors for the raw and the empirical-Bayes rankings; neither is stable, the empirical-Bayes one is marginally less unstable. Source: b4_eb_ranking.json

figures.title: b5 stability scatter
figures.caption: Corridor mean log ratio in the first half of the period against the second half, 807 corridors testable in both; rank correlation 0.91. Source: b5_stability.json

figures.title: Figure 1 gap ratio distribution
figures.caption: Realised over planned time on 26,369 OD legs; 98.3% exceed the plan, median 2.00×. Clipped at 8× for display. Source: w1_leg_summary.csv

figures.title: Figure 2 corridor audit
figures.caption: Welch tests on log time ratios, Benjamini-Hochberg at 5%: 273 corridors significantly slower, 512 faster, of 1,130 with >=10 legs. Source: w2_corridor_audit.csv

figures.title: Figure 3 top bottlenecks
figures.caption: The 15 highest excess ratios among corridors confirmed slower. Source: w2_top20_bottlenecks.csv

figures.title: Figure 4 support instability
figures.caption: Top-20 bottleneck lists at a 10-leg and a 30-leg support floor share 0 corridors. Sources: w2_top20_bottlenecks.csv, w2_corridor_audit_support30.csv

figures.title: Figure 5 model mae
figures.caption: Test-split MAE. The bar is the per-corridor median (33.04), not the mean, because MAE is minimised by the median. Sources: w7_model_metrics_v2_stepsize.csv, w7_model_metrics_v2.csv

figures.title: Figure 6 mae by support
figures.caption: Test MAE by how much history the corridor had. On unseen corridors 111.2 → 75.9 min; elsewhere the gain is 0.02-0.51 min. Source: w7_model_metrics_v2_stepsize.csv

figures.title: Figure 7 threshold sensitivity
figures.caption: Alerting across delay thresholds. The logistic classifier holds MCC 0.507-0.540 while the share of legs alerted falls 98% to 49%; the stream's own flag is weaker at every threshold. Source: w5_threshold_sensitivity.csv

figures.title: Figure 8 scale runtime
figures.caption: network_baseline and corridor_aggregate imported unchanged; wall time includes each run's parquet scan. Source: w7_scale_benchmark.json

figures.title: Figure 9 severity precision
figures.caption: Notification precision by computed severity over the earliest 2,000 replayed legs, scored with the history each leg had at its own time; hollow markers are the first, leaked measurement (D-054). Sources: w8_replay_leakage.json, w6_exception_eval.json

figures.title: Figure  architecture
figures.caption: System architecture: batch audit and models, streaming replay and serving, and the agent layer. No data behind it.

figures.title: Figure  b8 severity ci
figures.caption: Notification precision by severity grade with Wilson 95% intervals, as measured with as-of history, against alerting on every leg. Source: b8_exception_stats.json

figures.title: Figure  forest delta mae
figures.caption: MAE minus the back-off bar by slice for the reported (LightGBM) and served (Spark) models, with day-block 95% intervals; the unseen-corridor slice (about -32 minutes) is omitted for scale. Source: b2_significance.json

figures.title: Figure  rolling origin
figures.caption: MAE by rolling-origin fold (train on all earlier days, test on the next three): the back-off bar, the reported single-node model and, once its folds have run, the served Spark model. Sources: b2_rolling_origin_zoo.json, b2_rolling_origin.json
